rv.q: But “Skates,” alas, lacks comparable veracity, wit and skills of characterization.
If you're looking for light, fluffy musical fun combined with powerhouse vocals and tons of belting, SKATES is worth a spin.
The biggest strength of Skates is the pleasantly mainstream rock score, with nods to doo-wop, R&B, soul, and punk.
In the end, “Skates” goes absolutely everywhere you expect it to and nowhere you don’t, without enough wit or craft to make it worth the ride.
This not to be missed musical is showing off the newly remodeled Studebaker Theater, now a lovely updated state-of-the-art venue right on Michigan Avenue.
With the second act, which brought a stronger narrative, Skates is a refreshing blast from the past and a groovy way to spend an evening.
Like mindlessly binging on old TV shows from the seventies, it makes for a perfectly pleasant and forgettable two hours and change.
I for one, consider this a "work in progress" and since Covid slowed down that progression of learning, they will now make changes along the way.

cn.t: This nostalgic '70s roller-skating musical featuring American Idol alums Diana DeGarmo and Ace Young draws mixed reviews, with critics praising the powerhouse vocals but finding the female empowerment story underdeveloped.
